checks.finding: REQ-001/AC-001 require the taxonomy to name 'CLI returns malformed output' with a stated exit code, verdict-file production, and gate propagation, but no artifact in scope establishes current runner behaviour for this mode. investigation.md's quoted excerpt of run-panelist-gpt.sh:216-220 shows only an exit-code check, no output-shape validation, and INV-001/INV-002 document only 'absent CLI' and 'non-zero exit'. It is therefore unclear whether documenting 'malformed output' means writing down existing (unshown) behaviour, or requires NEW validation logic that REQ-002/REQ-003 never mention and Non-goals never excludes. The scope boundary between 'document existing behaviour' and 'implement new behaviour' is drawn clearly for the timeout and the absent/error path but not for this one taxonomy row. Two implementers would reasonably diverge on both the exit code written and whether new code is needed at all.

Two acceptance criteria are read down by their own tests to something weaker than the requirement text promises. (1) REQ-001 demands three things per failure mode (exit code, whether a verdict file is produced, propagation to the gate verdict). AC-001 already narrows to two, dropping the verdict-file element. TEST-001 narrows further, asserting only the presence of the five mode names and an exit code adjacent to each -- the propagation assertion is gone entirely. (2) AC-009 contains an internal tension: it demands a stated trust assumption and at least one mitigation per surface, then narrows its own verification to a literal-string search for the surface's identifier -- a method that confirms only that a token appears somewhere, not that a trust assumption or mitigation accompanies it. TEST-009 implements exactly that weak reading, so a document that name-drops hooks.state in an unrelated sentence would pass while never satisfying REQ-005's substance. In both cases an implementer optimizing to the executable AC/test text produces a document that passes review while retaining exactly the unverified-claim gap REQ-006 exists to close.

Two material negative paths implied by the requirements' own chosen mechanism are untested. (1) Edge Case 1 commits to a polled deadline mechanism precisely because timeout(1) is unavailable. A polling loop is not atomic with process completion: the CLI can exit successfully in the same interval the poller is about to declare the deadline exceeded. Edge Case 3 addresses only 'CLI killed mid-write', not this boundary race, and TEST-004/005/006 all use SDD_PANELIST_TIMEOUT=1 against a stub that sleeps 30s -- a huge margin that only exercises the unambiguous 'clearly hung' case. (2) The Assumptions section anticipates a CLI that ignores SIGTERM, but TEST-004's stub is a plain sleep command, which terminates on the very first SIGTERM by default disposition -- no test sub-case ever forces the SIGKILL-escalation branch, so a buggy or absent escalation implementation would still pass every specified test.

REQ-004 requires docs/THREAT-MODEL.md to carry 'an OWASP LLM Top 10 mapping and an MCP security cross-reference.' investigation.md's Open Questions for #134 explicitly flags the second element unresolved. This is never answered in requirements.md's Assumptions section. Consequently REQ-004's 'MCP security cross-reference' half has zero corresponding acceptance criterion: AC-007/AC-008 test only the OWASP table, and TEST-007/TEST-008 confirm the same -- no TEST anywhere tests an MCP security cross-reference. Unlike the SIGTERM/SIGKILL assumption, which IS explicitly deferred to design, this one is neither resolved nor flagged as a decision needed -- it is simply silently required and then untested, so an implementer could satisfy every stated AC for REQ-004 while omitting the MCP cross-reference entirely.

The requirements do change runtime behaviour and add SDD_PANELIST_TIMEOUT despite both source issues being labelled documentation, but this is not a quietly-assumed new approval boundary. BL-005, grounded in INV-017's direct read of guard-invariants.generated.js:5, confirms none of this feature's targets is in PROTECTED_GATE_SUFFIXES, so the repository's own human-copy governance trigger was affirmatively checked and correctly does not apply. The consequence of a timeout is REQ-003's explicit reuse of the already-existing absent/error mechanism, including its already-documented 'unless the task is explicitly waived' human override, so no new unwaivable gate is created. The bound is environment-configurable following an established repository convention, making the value operator-overridable rather than an irreversible unilateral decision.

REQ-004's 'MCP security cross-reference' clause has no acceptance criterion, no test, and no resolved Open Question. A design/implementation-policy reviewer inheriting this specification would have to invent, unguided, what 'MCP security cross-reference' concretely means for this repository -- which checklist to cite, what format it takes, what would count as satisfying it -- since nothing in the reviewed artifacts answers this and no acceptance criterion would catch an implementation that omits it entirely.

No domain/ directory, domain/context-map.md, or domain/domain-contract.json is referenced anywhere in the reviewed specification artifacts, and none of the documents declares a Bounded-Context field. Recorded as skipped per the check's explicit skip condition.
